examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola Given the Vertex and Another Point
examples.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(2,-2)$ and passes through the point $(-6,2).$
examples.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h, k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h, k) = (2,-2),$ we substitute $h=2$ and $k=-2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(-6, 2),$ so we can substitute $x=-6$ and $y=2$ into the equation above and solve for $p\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ (2+2)^{2} & =4p(-6-2) \\ 16 & =-32p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+2)^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{2})(x-2) \\ (y+2)^{2} & =-2(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041337/assets/c88e54f2a7acec3815a53fa4b0d641dd370ccf708b876f8dd231f05e115ea6fc.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
feedback.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the right. The parabola has its vertex at $(3,3)$ and passes through the point $(6,-3).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(3,3),$ we substitute $h=3$ and $k=3$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-3)^{2} & =4p(x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(6,-3),$ so we can substitute $x=6$ and $y=-3$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-3)^{2} & =4p(x-3) \\ (-3-3)^{2} & =4p(6-3) \\ 36 & =12p \\ p & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-3)^{2} & =4p(x-3) \\ (y-3)^{2} & =4(3)(x-3) \\ (y-3)^{2} & =12(x-3).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=3$ is positive.
